body.statement: For every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) or \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\), positivity of the selected table and \(c=P_{\vartheta}(S=1)>0\) imply \(P_{\vartheta}(E=e,S=1)=c r_e>0\) and therefore \(m_e=P_{\vartheta}(E=e)\ge c r_e>0\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\). Consequently, a nonempty design-A fiber forces the supplied observed margin vector \(m\) to lie in \(\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\), and every compatible design-B SCM induces positive population margins.
body.justification: Population-margin positivity is a compatibility implication of observed positivity and positive selection mass, not an independent maintained condition.
body.gap: The anchor imposes positive quantities in its regular formulas but does not isolate this elementary full-fiber compatibility consequence.
body.consumer: The cycle lift and residual-forest theorem may use positive margin ratios without strengthening either design's assumptions.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\vartheta\) in either full fiber.  By the definition of \(r\) and selected-table positivity,
\[
r_e=\sum_{w,z}p_{ewz}>0\qquad(e\in\mathcal E).
\]
The definition \(c=P_{\vartheta}(S=1)>0\) and the identity
\(P_{\vartheta}(E=e\mid S=1)=r_e\) give
\[
P_{\vartheta}(E=e,S=1)
=P_{\vartheta}(S=1)P_{\vartheta}(E=e\mid S=1)
=c r_e>0.
\]
Since \(\{E=e,S=1\}\subseteq\{E=e\}\), monotonicity of probability yields
\[
m_e=P_{\vartheta}(E=e)\ge P_{\vartheta}(E=e,S=1)=c r_e>0.
\]
In design A the equality \(P_{\vartheta}(E)=m\) is part of the definition of \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), so a nonempty fiber forces the supplied \(m\) to be in \(\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\).  In design B, \(m\) denotes the margin induced by \(P_{\vartheta}\), and the same calculation proves that every one of its coordinates is positive.
